summary: Practise evidence handling, integrity checks and financial-case chronology. Explore the five-day intermediate course outline.
lede: Chain of custody and digital forensics help financial-crime investigators preserve and examine electronic evidence for case findings. This course is for investigators, forensic analysts and case leads who need to document evidence handling, verify file integrity with SHA-256, reconstruct timelines from transaction and access records, and report findings with their limitations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for practitioners who collect, preserve, examine or review digital evidence in financial-crime cases. It suits intermediate-level professionals with familiarity with investigations or evidence handling.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with financial-crime investigations or digital evidence handling is recommended. No coding is required. Digital acquisition and volatile-data topics receive operational-planning coverage; the course does not require forensic software installation.
